analysis.title: Europe Open - Blue skies ahead
key_insights: Democrats won control of the Senate and House. AP has called 53 Senate seats for them with 5 still open (DDHQ projects 56), and 223 House seats called (majority 218) with about 80 still to be called.

Overnight risk-off after the sweep largely reversed. Nasdaq futures fell as much as -2.3% to -2.5% and recovered to -0.5% at print. US 10s are up only +3bp versus +7bp earlier. USD bottomed and JPY and CHF hold most G10 safe-haven gains.

The sharpest risk-off trigger was Gina Hinojosa's Texas governor win. She campaigned for a moratorium on new data center development until permanent state rules exist, which raised AI slowdown and data center buildout risk.

Citi's D1 salesperson reads the quick reversal as a sign that much of the AI negativity was already priced, and expects re-grossing through the European morning. The D1 desk is inclined to buy European weakness.

The Treasury Quarterly Refunding Announcement at 13:30 GMT is seen as a larger driver for Treasuries than the midterms. Citi expects $3bn cuts each to 20y and 30y auction sizes, out of consensus, which should weigh on USD.
Citi Economics no longer expects further RBNZ tightening after weaker NZ jobs data (unemployment 5.7%, an 11-year high). It expects the OCR on hold at 2.75% through 2027.
Riksbank decision at 08:30 GMT: Citi tentatively expects a 25bp hike with balanced guidance, and flags a dovish-framing risk to EURSEK shorts.
Eurozone October flash HICP is expected at 4.0% YoY (Citi, above the initial 3.9% forecast), core 2.5%. Headline is 50bp above ECB forecasts, which Citi says justifies another 25bp hike in December.
Brent is at $103. Trump told the FT the US has no immediate plans to strike Iran, and Tehran and Washington are reviewing mediators' proposals. Gold bounced 2% off the $4000 level.

A dovish QRA surprise could weigh on USD, and escalation risk with Iran remains.
A dovish Riksbank framing is a risk to EURSEK shorts.
A Labour win in the NZ election could restore the RBNZ's dual mandate.
A tight South Africa local election with possible recounts, with final results taking 48-72 hours.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq futures fell as much as -2.5% overnight and recovered to -0.5%. Citi's D1 salesperson says the risk reversal suggests the AI negativity was largely priced, with re-grossing possible through the European morning.
Recent de-grossing hit the names in the CGDORBND Index, which could benefit if flows return to Financials, Semis and Electrification.
Asia eTrading volumes ran 2.2x the 30-day averages, cooling slightly at print.
Systematics have been trimming rate shorts, per a Citi Rates Liquidity & Flows piece in the Best of Wire list.
geopolitical: US midterm results: Democrats won the Senate and House, flipping 7 Senate states including Texas, Kansas and Ohio.
Trump said the US has no immediate plans to strike Iran, though he is 'locked and loaded'. Tehran and Washington are reviewing mediators' proposals.
South Africa local elections: the ANC is no longer the organizing center of local politics, and coalition partners matter.
New Zealand election on Saturday: a Labour win could restore the RBNZ's dual mandate.
